site_program: 12 hospitals in the Valencia health area
screening_population: newborns with normal fetal ultrasound and normal delivery-room physical examination
screening_algorithm_raw: pre/postductal pulse oximetry; positive screen followed by clinical evaluation/echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: critical congenital heart defect screening; three positive-screen CCHD cases were total anomalous pulmonary venous return
diagnosis_categories_raw: total anomalous pulmonary venous return; early-onset sepsis with respiratory distress
diagnosis_counts_raw: TAPVR 3; early-onset sepsis with respiratory distress 2
individual_diagnoses: CCHD: TAPVR x3; CCHD-negative: early-onset sepsis with respiratory distress x2
management_actionability_evidence: The two CCHD-negative infants had early-onset sepsis with respiratory distress and would otherwise have been discharged home; the positive pulse-oximetry screen led to neonatal intensive care admission. This is a documented acute disposition/escalation consequence.
poolability_reason: harmonized denominator and Strict numerator fully classified; 100% ascertainment
source_full_text_provenance: Primary full text: Cubells E et al. Int J Neonatal Screen. 2018;4(1):3. PMID 33072929; PMCID PMC7548888; DOI 10.3390/ijns4010003
extraction_notes: Strict CAN-CCHD 2/2. Acute NICU admission attributable to the screening pathway supports CAN-A classification.

screening_population: term infants without known CCHD diagnosis
screening_algorithm_raw: AAP CCHD algorithm: immediate fail for saturation <90%; otherwise up to 3 tests; retrospective review of birth hospital and sole pediatric cardiac center
study_target_definition_raw: AAP critical congenital heart disease screening; one true-positive total anomalous pulmonary venous return
diagnosis_categories_raw: significant non-CCHD disease; remaining false positives without significant non-CCHD disease
diagnosis_counts_raw: significant non-CCHD disease 10; other/non-significant false positives 23
individual_diagnoses: individual non-CCHD diagnoses not available in the accessible primary text
management_actionability_evidence: The accessible primary report states that 10/33 false positives had significant non-CCHD disease but does not document specific treatment, escalation, disposition change, or required follow-up for those 10. 'Significant disease' alone is insufficient for Strict CAN-CCHD under the locked Protocol Core.
entry_hold_reason: Phase 4.5 shorthand 'exact actionable numerator 10/33' requires correction: primary-source actionability is not demonstrated in accessible text
poolability_reason: denominator and broad clinically relevant outcome are complete, but Strict actionability cannot be released without management evidence from the primary report
source_full_text_provenance: Primary article abstract/journal text reverified: Diller CL et al. Pediatrics. 2018;141(5):e20174065. PMID 29691284; DOI 10.1542/peds.2017-4065. Full article text not accessible in current retrieval pass.
extraction_notes: Provisional Strict CAN-CCHD 0/33; Expanded CAN-CCHD 10/33; aggregate NON_CAN 23/33. The 23 are not assumed healthy or transitional; they are the study-defined remainder without significant non-CCHD disease.

site_program: tertiary-care hospital; Well Baby Unit plus NICU
screening_population: newborns >34 weeks and >1.5 kg; included Well Baby Unit and NICU; very sick/mechanically ventilated infants excluded
screening_timing_raw: pulse oximetry at birth, 24 h and 48 h; abnormal result repeated after 1 h
screening_algorithm_raw: SpO2 <=94% considered abnormal; repeat after 1 h; persistent abnormality led to echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: study target was congenital heart disease broadly rather than the review's harmonized CCHD target
diagnosis_categories_raw: structural CHD among 8 pulse-positive infants; PPHN; congenital pneumonia
diagnosis_counts_raw: pulse-positive structural CHD 8; PPHN 6; congenital pneumonia 2
individual_diagnoses: pulse-only CHD: TGA; pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum. Pulse+clinical CHD: TOF; pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum; DORV/VSD; ASD/CAVSD/pulmonary stenosis/PDA; CAVSD/DORV/pulmonary atresia; critical pulmonary stenosis. CCHD-negative candidates before harmonized mapping: PPHN x6; congenital pneumonia x2.
management_actionability_evidence: The source identifies PPHN and congenital pneumonia among eight pulse-positive infants without study-defined CHD, but does not document diagnosis-specific treatment, escalation, disposition change, or required follow-up. Generic counselling/appropriate management language is insufficient for Strict actionability. Mixed Well Baby Unit/NICU population also requires sensitivity handling unless separable.
entry_hold_reason: broad CHD study target requires lesion-by-lesion harmonized CCHD mapping; mixed Well Baby/NICU population requires heterogeneity/sensitivity flag
poolability_reason: primary denominator cannot be frozen until all eight structural lesions are mapped to the review's harmonized CCHD target; subsequent poolability must also account for mixed nursery/NICU setting
source_full_text_provenance: Primary full text: Mohsin M et al. Cureus. 2019;11(6):e4808. PMID 31403007; PMCID PMC6682379; DOI 10.7759/cureus.4808. Lesion identities extracted from the article's diagnostic flow figure.
extraction_notes: The article's reported 8 'true positives' are CHD broadly, not automatically harmonized CCHD. Do not set denominator=8 until the locked lesion mapping is restored/applied. PPHN6+pneumonia2 are raw diagnoses only and are not automatically Strict CAN-CCHD.
